checks.reason: For the supported canonical inventory tree, root '.' now has depth zero and every nonroot directory is ordered by its number of path components. A child directory therefore has strictly greater depth than its parent and is computed first under descending depth. Byte-order tie breaking only orders unrelated equal-depth directories. The existing child serialization uses each already computed directory digest, so the previous root/top-level tie and null child digest are removed. The unchanged byte-order sorting of immediate child records preserves deterministic canonical child arrays.

The historical RED log was read and shows six methods, three assertion failures and no errors/skips: root inclusion of a child digest, an empty child's digest, and propagation to root. The auditor independently reran all six permanent tests on Python 3.14.6 and 3.9.6; each suite passed with zero skips. Four tests use exact literal canonical child arrays plus direct hashlib, and two test propagation/order properties. The added one-method pure holdout spells a separate tree with an empty sibling, a direct root file, a Unicode directory and its deeper child. It independently computes explicit immediate-child arrays with standard JSON/hashlib and checks every exact directory digest for two same-length descendant hashes and reversed input order. The changed branch and root change while the unrelated empty sibling remains stable. This holdout passed with filesystem-call guards and does not reuse the producer's canonical, hash or depth helpers as its expected-value oracle.

The auditor reversed only the new depth expression and two added comment lines in memory, without writing the source. The resulting SHA-256 exactly matched the previously accepted builder caa1c98d02190c18c4fad6cd354a812dc4b06d86d99768773b6169cd2b18d0db, proving no additional source change is hidden in this delta. Independent current runs passed 19 descriptor/confinement tests, 18 source-bound Validator tests, 15 synthetic E2E tests and 15 guarded migration/lineage tests, all with zero skips. Thus previously accepted active-ancestor invalidation, no-follow reads, explicit source authority, field/hash binding and caller/migration regressions remain exercised on this combined source state. These are bounded synthetic compatibility results rather than expanded product certification.
